newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PNG stocks jump after Chan stands aside as PM.
newsitem.headline: PNG stocks jump after Chan stands aside as PM.

text.p: Papua New Guinea-linked stocks jumped in active early Thursday trade after PNG Prime Minister Julius Chan stood aside to resolve 10 days of political turmoil in Port Moresby caused by the hiring of mercenaries.
Orogen Minerals Ltd, which is 51 percent owned by the PNG government, was up 13 cents to A$3.15 by 10.30 a.m. (2330 GMT), while Oil Search Ltd rose 11 cents to A$2.68 on volume of 539,323 shares.

Lihir Gold Ltd rose six cents to A$2.19 while Niugini Mining Ltd was unchanged at A$2.95 on four trades totalling 20,000. Bougainville Copper Ltd rose five cents to 60 cents on volume of 540,000 shares traded.

"It's positive that Chan's resigned and it should calm the situation up there somewhat," said ANZ Securities gold analyst David Kauler. "It is a cheap time to be buying some of those PNG stocks, particularly Lihir on the gold side," Kauler said.
But some investors would remain tentative in the next six months while a new government was elected and its resources policy was formed, he said.

There was currently no suggestion of restricting foreign companies, as the political instability was linked to the use of mercenaries and perceptions of corruption rather than the presence of foreign miners, Kauler said.
"There's been no suggestion that resources policy should change," he said.

"This latest saga really hasn't had a lot to do with foreign companies operating their resources projects in PNG, it's had more to do with the issue of hiring mercenaries to kill PNG nationals," he said.
PNG retailer and trader Collins and Leahy Ltd rose 25 cents to A$3.50.

Analysts said the next six months would remain a volatile period for overseas investment, but that PNG had an opportunity to convince foreign investors it could clean up its political and financial act.
"It's going to be a difficult, volatile period for investment in the country," Kauler said.
"You're going to see a fight between people who see a cheap buying opportunity and other people saying we don't know what the policy is going to be for six months, so let's steer clear," he said.
"Everyone is relieved that the parliamentary process actually worked and that we didn't go into a period of military control," said ABN AMRO Hoare Govett Head of Mining Research David Walker said.
"The expectation that the mid-year elections can be brought forward and that there can be an orderly resolution of the impasse has been accepted well," Walker said.
He said however that any new government would be forced to reassess its poor fiscal position and look to increase taxes, possibly even the 1.25 percent mining royalty.
"I suspect that what you're going to see is a potential increase in charges and maybe taxation to try and tackle some of the fiscal imbalances up there," he said.
Opinion was divided over whether the end of PNG crisis would allow Highlands Gold Ltd's plan to raise A$190 million in a float of a separate company, Highlands Pacific Ltd, to go ahead on schedule.
"Highlands Pacific is going to struggle to get their float away," ANZ's Kauler said, adding a delay was inevitable.
Walker however said the float appeared to be on track.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
